newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin seeks IPB selloff first - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin seeks IPB selloff first - CTK.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Friday he would submit a plan to the government for the further privatisation of the country's four largest banks within 14 days, the Czech agency CTK reported.
It quoted him as telling a meeting of business managers that he would suggest that shares of Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB) should be the first to be privatised.
"I will recommend that (the privatisation plan) begin with the privatisation of Investicni a Postovni Banka," Kocarnik told the conference of the Central European Management Association.
Last week, Kocarnik said the government must quickly formulate a strategy for privatising state-held shares in the country's four largest banks.

Analysts have been calling for the further privatisation of the so-called "Big Four", which control over 70 percent of Czech banking activity, as a way to bring more efficiency and competition to the banking sector.

The four banks are Ceska Sporitelna a.s., Komercni Banka a.s., and IPB -- which have had some shares privatised through the government's voucher selloffs -- and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. which is controlled through a variety of Czech and Slovak state institutions.

Kocarnik said last week several international investment banks including JP Morgan, Merrill Lynch and Salomon Brothers had been lobbying him during a recent visit to Washington, pushing for the further privatisation of the Big Four.
